what: Worker count x games-in-flight, and simulations vs generation size.
why: The plan's full8x8 profile (2500 games, 300 simulations) assumed a data-centre GPU. These are the numbers that replaced that assumption on the hardware the project actually has.

worker_sweep.note: 8 workers is slower than 6: they contend for one small GPU and for cores. More is not better past the knee.

simulation_sweep.note: Positions per game is ~58.5 throughout, so simulations trade almost linearly against games. 10 workers at 300 sims measured 0.181 games/s -- worse than 6.

T23_workers_over_stage2.why: The criterion assumed 8 cores and a GPU with headroom. Six processes on one 4 GB laptop GPU contend for it. The practical target it existed to protect -- a generation inside 20 minutes -- is met by adjusting games_per_generation instead. A central inference server (plan P2) would combine the workers' small batches into large ones and is the thing that would close this.

CORRECTION.what_was_wrong: The simulation_sweep below used 36-48 games spread over 6 workers, so each worker got 6-8 games and its games_in_flight collapsed to that -- a worker cannot hold more games in flight than it was given. The sweep therefore measured batches of ~6 while reporting a setting of 24, and every rate in it is roughly 2.4x too low.
CORRECTION.what_it_changes: A generation is 12.2 minutes, not the 25 the config comment claims -- comfortably inside the 20-minute target. 300 simulations would be roughly 17.5 minutes and is therefore also affordable, which reverses the trade made in configs/full8x8.yaml. Left at 200 for the current run; worth revisiting for the next one.
CORRECTION.lesson: Benchmark at the batch size you intend to run, not a smaller one. The harness silently shrinks games_in_flight to the number of games available, which is correct behaviour and made the measurement mean something other than what it said.
